12 Jan 2024, -3°C, Astra wouldn't crank outside the house at 6:10, just a click and the dash lights flickering. Battery was a Varta from when I bought the car in 2019. Neighbour Pete (no. 41) brought his Skoda Octavia round and we jumped it with my Ring 400A booster leads. Order: red on the flat battery +, red on the donor +, black on the donor -, black on a bare metal earth point on the engine (the lifting eye), NOT the flat battery's - terminal, keeps any spark away from the battery. Ran Pete's car 5 minutes first, then ours started first go. Removed the leads in reverse order. Left it idling 30 min, then drove to the job the long way. Multimeter the next evening after sitting all day: 12.1V resting, which is about 50% charge, so the battery was done. Replaced with a Bosch S4 005 (type 063, 60Ah, 540A CCA) from Euro Car Parts, £89.99, order ECP-2204417. Old one went back for the £10 core refund. After swapping: reset the one-touch electric windows (hold the switch up 3 seconds) and the clock. Related: [[Dashboard warning lights]], [[Winter tyres]], [[Road trip car checklist]] (leads now live in the boot permanently).
